subject: gov.legislate
name: Critical-infrastructure protection legal framework
milestone: Adopted unanimously by the National Assembly 2026-08-20
position_end: Law n° 25/2026 on the protection of critical information infrastructure and digital security was adopted unanimously by the National Assembly on 2026-08-20, seven days after reaching its intercommission. On the ministry's account it grades obligations by risk - ordinary networks and systems on standard requirements, critical infrastructure on enhanced ones covering monitoring, data backup, encryption of sensitive information, business continuity and disaster recovery, and regular resilience testing - establishes a National Cybersecurity Authority, a national computer emergency response team, sectoral teams and cybersecurity operations services, mandates in-country storage of state-sensitive data, and folds in technology-neutral standards for the AI era and the child-online-protection plan PAPEL. No promulgation date, gazette reference or text is published
sources: 2026-08-20-seneweb-loi-securite-numerique-adoption|2026-08-20-el-malick-ndiaye-cybersecurite-culture-administrative|2026-08-17-senegal-critical-infrastructure-bill-ministry-details|2026-07-30-arcop-cybersecurite-marches-infrastructures-critiques|2026-07-15 Senegal pushes stronger cybersecurity cooperation to protect critical infrastructure|2026-08-13-senegal-critical-infrastructure-bill-bacary-sarr|2026-08-14-senegal-moves-to-safeguard-digital-infrastructure|2026-08-14-senegal-critical-infrastructure-cybersecurity-bill|2026-08-14-senegal-moves-to-strengthen-critical-infrastructure-and-digital-security
note: every provision is the ministry's own description; the bill text is not held, and the base held nothing on this workstream at the window's start. During the adoption debate the Assembly's first vice-president argued cybersecurity must become a standing administrative culture rather than a compliance exercise, calling for mandatory staff training, professional-only communication channels and minimum device-security standards - which is an account of where the state's own practice stands rather than of what the law requires

position_start: A memorandum signed, nothing on record being built
position_end: A memorandum signed, nothing on record being built
sources: 2024-10-04 Senegal launches sovereign cloud initiative with Google
note: no build, siting, capacity or spend reported in the twelve months to 2026-08-06, while a different partner is reported as having deployed and tested; the base does not establish how the two relate

subject: infra.store
name: Internet exchange point reactivation
milestone: Announced in a state-operator partnership, 2025-03-26
position_end: Announced for reactivation, no date; no traffic, membership or operating statement since
note: the only source in the base naming the exchange

subject: infra.store
name: National cloud infrastructure
milestone: Formally received 24 March 2026
position_end: Formally received to host the strategic applications of the 2026 Youth Olympic Games, built on a Chinese vendor's stack under a contract signed in July 2025 and stated to guarantee local hosting of sensitive data; beyond the Games the ministry states it lays the foundations of a national public cloud, with 200 cloud engineers to be trained and a technology centre of excellence created

subject: infra.store
name: Off-site backup written into procurement
milestone: Offers due 25 June 2026
position_end: A road agency's open procurement requires the successful bidder to guarantee data localisation in Senegal, manage backups with tested restoration procedures, hold Tier 3 redundant data centres in Senegal, assure real-time replication and put continuity and disaster-recovery solutions in place naming a replication site in Senegal, under signed availability service levels; it is a stated requirement covering one agency, not an award or an operating facility

subject: infra.store
name: PAIX Dakar data centre
milestone: Groundbreaking 2025-01-23
position_start: Under construction, 1.2 MW and 918 square metres, targeted operational in 2026
position_end: Under construction; no commissioning, energisation or opening on file at 2026-08-06
sources: 2025-01-23 PAIX Data Centres breaks ground on Dakar data center|2025-01-27-paix-dakar-data-center-connectingafrica
note: the target year has not expired, so this is not recorded as stalled

subject: infra.store
name: State data-centre estate
milestone: Three sites totalling 1,424 TB, the oldest 81% and the second 93% used
position_end: Three state data centres: one built 2004 at 32 TB and 81% used, one built 2008 at 392 TB and 93% used, and the 2021 national centre at 1,000 TB and 31% used, costing 83 billion FCFA; 176 structures host data there. None of the three is designated a secondary, mirrored or disaster-recovery facility for the others, and no off-site backup arrangement is stated
note: the operator's institutional page states 2,500 TB in total against the 1,424 TB this breakdown carries

subject: infra.energy
name: Diass battery energy storage
milestone: Groundbreaking 31 March 2026, 56 MW / 56 MWh
position_end: Groundbreaking on a 56 MW / 56 MWh battery storage system, framed by the utility as the start of a structural transformation toward stable and sovereign electricity; the storage is not in service at the date of the record and no reliability figure accompanies it

subject: infra.energy
name: Grid reliability indices
milestone: Unserved energy 0.29%, interruption frequency 9.12, interruption duration 6h40 against a 1h30 norm
position_start: Unserved energy 0.22%, interruption frequency 8.4, interruption duration 7h19 (2023)
position_end: For 2024 the regulator reports unserved energy at 15.79 GWh, 0.29% of energy sold, within the 0.5% norm but worse than 2023; interruption frequency at 9.12 per customer a year, within the norm of 10 but worse than the 8.4 of 2023; and interruption duration at 6h40 against a norm of 1h30, so the norm was not met though it improved on 7h19. A nationwide power cut on 12 September 2024 followed an incident at a 90 kV substation, and the regulator records that operators did not supply all 2024 data

subject: infra.energy
name: Power provision for data-centre and telecom infrastructure
status: Implemented, a priced supply route with no continuity or priority commitment
milestone: 2026 tariff grids in force from 1 January 2026
position_end: A regulated high-voltage route exists and is priced, including a distinct standby tariff at 95.12 FCFA a kilowatt-hour off-peak and 144.49 at peak against a general tariff of 71.43 and 108.52; no guaranteed volume, continuity commitment, priority-load status for telecommunications or data centres, and no water provision, is established
note: the only Senegal-specific statement is an industry recommendation of December 2025 that telecommunications be recognised as critical national infrastructure and brought into the energy programme, with no adoption recorded

subject: infra.energy
name: Rural electrification
milestone: Second-phase contract signed 23 July 2026 for at least 753 villages
position_start: Rural electrification at 64.5% against urban at 97.1%, with universal access moved from 2025 to 2029
position_end: A second-phase contract signed in July 2026 for the electrification of at least 753 villages, 183 solar mini-power-stations, connections including household internal wiring and about 5% of financing to income-generating activities; the first phase, launched in 2019 with an initial target of 300 villages, completed in November 2025. Grid densification works started in five lots with 39 km of lines constructed at December 2025 against a June 2027 target of 3,470 km, and a regional additional financing appraised in March 2026 names delays in resettlement planning in Senegal as a significant constraint

subject: infra.capacity
name: Data centres operating in Senegal
milestone: A continental count at mid-2025
position_end: Seven at mid-2025, level with Ghana, against South Africa's 56, Kenya's 19 and Nigeria's 17
note: a reference-study figure, cited and not absorbed; the base holds no Senegalese primary count and no capacity figure

subject: infra.capacity
name: State capacity to deliver its own digital programme
milestone: Development objective and implementation progress both downgraded in May 2025
position_start: Development objective rated moderately satisfactory to May 2025
position_end: Both the development objective and implementation progress downgraded to moderately unsatisfactory: the $35 million capacity component rated the same with no tangible progress, the enterprise-architecture feasibility firm only now being selected, the state fibre audit still incomplete at 28 January 2026 against a December 2027 target, specialist recruitments significantly delayed and the project coordinator's contract not renewed in October 2025; against that, the minister stated in April 2026 an intention to train 100 cloud engineers with Chinese support ahead of the 2026 Games

subject: infra.cybersec
name: ITU Global Cybersecurity Index score
milestone: The 2024 edition
position_start: 67.17 out of 100, tier three of four (2024)
position_end: 67.17 out of 100, tier three of four; no newer edition held
sources: 2026-07-15 Senegal pushes stronger cybersecurity cooperation to protect critical infrastructure
note: a reference index, cited and not absorbed; the score predates the entire 2025-26 breach run

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National computer emergency response team
status: Implemented, scoped to the administrative intranet
milestone: Statutory architecture for a national team adopted 20 August 2026
position_end: The state digital operator runs a response team covering the administrative intranet alongside a security portal; the critical information infrastructure bill adopted on 20 August 2026 provides for a national cybersecurity authority, a national response team, sectoral teams and security operations centres, with no commencement date or implementing decree stated
note: a named expert stated on 2026-02-06 that Senegal has neither a national cybersecurity agency nor a national response team, and no evidence was found that either has since been established

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Procurement route for critical-infrastructure cybersecurity
milestone: Memorandum with a foreign cybersecurity supplier reported 2026-08-18
position_end: Three routes floated — a three-year standing supplier arrangement, functional rather than technical specifications, and pooled purchasing — with the digital economy ministry reported to have signed a memorandum with a United States cybersecurity firm that is seeking Senegalese partners; no timetable, contract value or affected system established
note: the state's own diagnosis locates the blockage in procurement, not in budget or capability; the memorandum's text, scope and value are not published

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Recorded cybercrime offences
position_end: 3,794 offences recorded (2025)
note: national police figures reported alongside an international police organisation's estimate of at least US$5bn in Africa-wide cyberattack losses in 2025; neither the recording basis nor a clear-up rate is stated

subject: infra.cybersec
name: State systems breached
milestone: Parliamentary hearings announced 2026-08-20
position_start: One held state breach on file, its date disputed
position_end: Three on file - the tax authority in 2025, the identity directorate on 2026-01-19 and the public treasury in May 2026 - with parliamentary hearings announced into further recent attacks naming the file-automation directorate and the tax and domains directorate
note: the treasury breach carries month precision only, and no technical accounting has been published for any of the three. On 2026-08-20, a day after the critical-infrastructure law's adoption, the National Assembly's president announced hearings of the state technical services and of the agencies hit, naming the Direction de l'automatisation des fichiers and the Direction générale des impôts et des domaines; neither the number of further incidents nor their dates is stated, so the count of three is what the base can still support

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Digital agency and health-cover platform interconnection
milestone: A convention announced 2026-07-23 committing the two bodies to interconnect their platforms
position_end: The convention signed, with training of service-point managers, joint communication and a monitoring mechanism committed
note: no enrolment target, go-live date or named data-sharing instrument, and the personal-data commitment is an intention not referred to the regulator

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Government enterprise architecture
milestone: Interim diagnostic results presented and the inventory of state information systems launched at a workshop, 2026-07-29
position_end: A framework being built across policies, processes, data, applications and infrastructure; the diagnostic phase's interim results have been presented, a target architecture proposed, and the inventory of state information systems launched
note: the inventory is the load-bearing commitment and, though now under way, carries no scope, deadline or publication commitment; implemented by the state digital agency with donor programme funding

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National climate-transparency data platform
milestone: The project launched in Dakar 2026-07-22, externally funded, running 42 months
position_start: A grant approval request on file, the project not started
position_end: Launched, with three components including a platform to centralise, harmonise, secure and publish climate data
note: the ministry names the defect directly: gaps in availability, quality, harmonisation and inter-sectoral sharing

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National interoperability platform
milestone: A government enterprise-architecture account names interoperability as a standing challenge and platforms as still siloed, sixteen months after launch
position_start: Launched 2025-04-22 with external support, a first phase targeted for end-December 2025
position_end: Still stated as an intention rather than a capability, with silos named by the state itself
note: no held source records the first phase completing on its end-2025 target

subject: dpi.exchange
name: PLANET 3 school management platform
milestone: Launched 3 October 2025 as the national norm
position_end: Launched as the national norm rather than an optional experiment, giving inspectors, head teachers, teachers, pupils and parents personalised interfaces with real-time data access, and built by the ministry's own developers; a head teacher and a United Nations regional director both named unstable connectivity, insufficient equipment and access difficulties at peak periods

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Senegal and Gambia customs data exchange
milestone: A second monitoring committee set a three-month roadmap on 2026-07-17
position_end: A roadmap agreed: the customs system installed at three border posts within three months, transit tracking, and interface data exchange once the system is live
note: agreed at operational level rather than by treaty; the clock started on 2026-07-17

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Unified social-protection information system
milestone: A two-day workshop opened 2026-07-23 to diagnose existing systems and settle interoperability and data governance
position_end: At diagnostic stage, with the minister stating each structure runs its own system and cannot share data
note: it covers five named social programmes; no budget, timeline or lead technical agency is reported, and data governance is an output of the workshop rather than an input

subject: dpi.id
name: Birth registration coverage among children
milestone: 58.98% of children in early-childhood structures held a civil-status document in 2025
position_start: 81.4% of children under five registered with the civil registry (2023 survey)
position_end: Of 186,744 children received in early-childhood development structures in 2025, 110,148 held a civil-status document — 58.98% — a different population from the 2023 household survey's 81.4% of under-fives registered, and the gap bars children from national examinations
note: the two figures are drawn from different populations and are not reconciled

subject: dpi.id
name: Civil-registration modernisation programme
milestone: A final steering committee held 2026-06-29, closing the externally funded programme
position_start: Running, with two implementing agencies and the national agency as counterpart
position_end: Closed on completion; outputs include 26 modern centres, 400 centres interconnected, 1,200 computers, a validated bill and a national civil-status strategy costed at FCFA 68bn
note: a programme closure rather than a capability closure, and the only EU governance instrument on file for Senegal

subject: dpi.id
name: Civil-status archive digitisation
milestone: The agency's own August 2025 presentation
position_start: 20m acts digitised and indexed against a 30m universe, 10m remaining (2025-08)
position_end: Still 20m of 30m; no later national figure is held
note: the June 2026 closing report gives 10m digitised and 20m indexed as two separate totals, unreconciled with the August 2025 reading

subject: dpi.id
name: Civil-status record digitisation
milestone: 20 million acts digitised, indexed and loaded
position_end: 20 million civil-status acts digitised, indexed and loaded into the national register, the central database reachable from the application deployed in 400 centres, with a user-facing platform built for remote requests; the agency ruled that the programme's tool is the only one government recognises and called on mayors running unauthorised software to stop

subject: dpi.id
name: Civil-status software deployment across centres
milestone: Agency figure given at African Civil Registration Day in Kaolack, 2026-08-10
position_start: 235 of about 400 centres connected and operational, 383 installed (2025-08)
position_end: 74% of civil-status centres fully deployed, up from 70% reported five days earlier, with the citizen-facing request service live in 189 communes; the agency launched phase four of its remediation plan on 10 August 2026, extending to Kaffrine and Tambacounda
note: the denominator behind the percentage is 629 centres; the agency's director-general frames civil registration as an instrument of sovereignty, and the same agency says its 2026 budget has not been notified

subject: dpi.id
name: Direction de l'Automatisation des Fichiers
milestone: Mandated under a 1977 decree; identity enrolment extending from Dakar commissariats since 2017
position_start: Managing the ministry of the interior's population files at a single processing centre
position_end: Managing the ministry of the interior's non-police population files at a single processing centre, conducting the studies and development of every ministry application, and producing the foreigner and refugee identity cards, firearm permits and telephone-subscriber identification alongside the biometric national card; biometric enrolment has extended progressively from named Dakar commissariats to the regions, certain gendarmerie brigades and sub-prefectures

subject: dpi.id
name: ECOWAS biometric identity card implementing decree
milestone: In force since 2016-09-29
position_start: Fixes the card number, prints the national identification number and makes the card serve as the voter card
position_end: Fixes a 17-digit card number, prints the national identification number on the reverse for electors and non-electors alike, carries the elector's number and polling details on the same card, and at article 2 makes the card serve as the voter card for citizens on the electoral roll

subject: dpi.id
name: Live civil-registration database load
milestone: The agency reported 15.3m records loaded
position_end: 15.3m civil-status records in the live national register
sources: 2026-07-15 Senegal digitizes more than 15 million birth records in civil registration overhaul
note: a subset of archive stock, not a replacement figure; English coverage calls them birth records where the agency's own term covers all events

subject: dpi.id
name: Mobile subscriber identification campaign
milestone: Unidentified lines terminated definitively from 29 September 2025
position_end: The final phase of the national subscriber identification campaign, run with the five operators and the interior ministry's file-automation directorate: unidentified lines suspended on 31 March 2025, terminated definitively from 29 September, with no regularisation accepted after 31 October 2025; whether verification queries the national file or only inspects the card is not stated

subject: dpi.id
name: National identity card production
milestone: Production resumed 2026-04-01 after a ransomware breach forced suspension on 2026-02-05
movement: No change, restored after a two-month suspension
position_start: Issuing; the biometric card made the sole accepted proof of identity for voter registration (2025-02)
position_end: Issuing again from 2026-04-01, with enrolment restarting progressively across centres and overseas missions
note: exfiltration is unrebutted and the directorate's communiqués assert integrity only, never confidentiality; the volume claim appears as both 139 GB and 139 TB in one actor's two artefacts

subject: dpi.id
name: Pension proof-of-life platform
milestone: Campaign opened 1 July 2026 for three months
position_end: A digital platform on which Senegalese pensioners complete periodic proof of life, requiring the ECOWAS national identity card, with assisted routes through a relative, mutual credit payment points, institution offices or mandated agents collecting at home — the identity credential made the entry condition of a large social-payment system

subject: dpi.id
name: State public key infrastructure and certificate services
milestone: Operated under the 2008 electronic transactions law and its certification decree
position_start: Issuing electronic certificates to users of the Senegalese administration
position_end: Issuing server and personal certificates for authentication, signature and encryption to users of the Senegalese administration, with registration, renewal, revocation, publication, archiving and key recovery, and centralised server-side signature; the service is scoped to administration users, and no citizen-facing single sign-on or identity-register verification interface is described

subject: dpi.id
name: Universal digital identity under the technology strategy
milestone: Single-window portal authenticating on the national identification number, launched 24 March 2026
position_end: The national identification number carried on the biometric card is the login key of the government single-window portal launched in March 2026, and the same card serves as the voter card under the 2016 implementing decree; the technology strategy targets more than 90% of Senegalese holding a digital identity by 2034, and no coverage figure against that target is published
note: announced and benchmarked against a neighbour's system in late 2025, with no held source recording a build, a pilot or an enrolment

subject: dpi.pay
name: Authorised electronic money issuers
milestone: 11 authorised initiatives at 30 September 2024
position_end: 11 authorised initiatives: three licensed issuers, eight banks issuing through a partnership or technical services provider, and one telecommunications operator, with no state treasury issuer unlike two neighbouring member states; the second-largest issuer count in the union

subject: dpi.pay
name: Central bank position on crypto-assets
milestone: Governors' round table at Dakar 8 May 2026
position_end: A stated orientation from a governors' round table convened at Dakar on financial stability, regulation, supervision, monetary sovereignty and consumer protection, and on payment-system interoperability; it announces no instrument, committee, timetable or union rule

subject: dpi.pay
name: Diaspora remittance flows
milestone: FCFA 2,211bn in 2024, about 12% of gross domestic product
position_end: FCFA 2,211bn in 2024 against an estimated FCFA 1,600bn in 2023, about 12% of gross domestic product and now exceeding official development assistance; the figures are attributed to the central bank through a press report rather than taken from its own publication, and establish the size of the flow rather than the channel it moves through

subject: dpi.pay
name: Digital payment share on the Dakar rapid-transit network
milestone: A super-app integrated into the network for ticketing and top-ups
position_start: 10% of payments digital, the prior figure undated in the source
position_end: 39% of payments digital (2026-07)
note: the prior figure carries no date; the network runs up to 300,000 passengers a day

subject: dpi.pay
name: Electronic payment of customs duties and taxes
milestone: Integrated into the customs information system
position_start: Electronic payment of duties and taxes, on-screen viewing of signed documents and electronic compilation of attachments
position_end: Electronic payment of duties and taxes, on-screen viewing of documents signed by the qualified authorities and electronic compilation of attachments, within a clearance chain in which no removal of goods may occur without payment, a consignment or a sufficient guarantee

subject: dpi.pay
name: Financial services mediation caseload
milestone: 475 disputed files in 2025 against 379 in 2024
position_end: 475 disputed files handled in 2025, a rise of nearly 25%: 357 in banking, microfinance, financial institutions and the post office and 118 in insurance against 71; the leading banking grounds are slow international transfers at 25.4%, shareholder premium claims at 19.1% and credit repayment difficulty at 17%, and no digital-payment complaint category is broken out at all

subject: dpi.pay
name: Instant payment platform participation
milestone: 13 Senegalese participants authorised at the 30 September 2025 launch
position_end: 13 Senegalese participants authorised to open the union's interoperable instant payment services to the public at launch, the largest count of the eight member states against 45 across the union; two named electronic money issuers are on the list and a third named issuer is not

subject: dpi.pay
name: Levy on mobile-money transfers
milestone: Proposed under a recovery plan to raise about FCFA 220bn over three years
position_end: Proposed and contested, with an industry body recommending it be dropped; no adoption, withdrawal or enactment on file at 2026-08-06
sources: 2025-12-08 GSMA maps the reforms required for Senegal's digital takeoff
note: both sources post-date the window's start, so the wiki cannot say what the proposal's position was in August 2025

subject: dpi.pay
name: SenTrésor state payments platform
milestone: Social benefits payable through an electronic money operator from 2 September 2026
position_start: Launched 2 June 2025 to digitise salaries, allowances, social aid, pensions and scholarships, with no beneficiary count published
position_end: The social security fund announced on 2 September 2026 that benefits can be paid through a named electronic money operator directly into a beneficiary's account without travelling, enrolment by a form available in every agency; no beneficiary count, first-payment date or statement of whether the route is optional is given

subject: dpi.pay
name: Share of monetary-union electronic money and microfinance assets
milestone: 29.7 per cent of union e-money outstandings at 31 December 2025
position_end: The country held 29.7 per cent of monetary-union electronic-money outstandings and 26.5 per cent of the union's large-microfinance assets at 31 December 2025, leading the region on both counts. Its CFAF 1,234.3 billion of microfinance assets is ahead of the next two members' CFAF 1,226.7 billion and CFAF 889.4 billion, the three together holding 71.9 per cent of the union's large-institution assets; it hosts 81 large institutions and 2.28 million of the union's 14.66 million accounts, 15.5 per cent of the total and up 15.2 per cent on the year. Union-wide electronic-money outstandings rose 35.2 per cent to CFAF 1,923.2 billion and accounts reached 172.9 million, of which only 60.6 million, 35.1 per cent, were active. The domestic market is a duopoly, one provider on close to 80 per cent at CFAF 459 billion against the other's 19 per cent at CFAF 106 billion
note: the union-wide active-account share of 35.1 per cent is the figure that qualifies the rest: leading the region on outstandings is compatible with most accounts being dormant, and no domestic active-account figure is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Share of regional mobile-money transaction volume
milestone: The central bank's 2024 annual report on digital financial services
position_end: 24.1% of union volume, the largest share, and 30.2% of transaction value, with the union's highest volume growth
note: both ends come from the same source's own series rather than from wiki movement; eleven electronic-money issuers operate in Senegal

subject: dpi.pay
name: Tax on money transfers
milestone: Loi 2025-17 of 27 September 2025 creating the tax
position_start: Planned, with no adoption, withdrawal or enactment on file
position_end: Enacted: new article 395 applies the tax to money-transfer operations carried out by any means leaving a trace, notably electronically and by mobile telephony; article 396 makes liable any person carrying out transfers plus banks, financial establishments and decentralised financial system firms; article 399 sets the rate at 0.5% capped at 2,000 FCFA a transaction; and article 397 exempts cash deposits, withdrawals up to 20,000 francs in 24 hours, bank transfers, intra-network transfers by payment service providers, state transfers, and salary or study-grant transfers

subject: dpi.pay
name: Tax payment through a mobile operator application
milestone: Opened on the operator's application
position_end: Payment of taxes, duties and fees opened through a mobile operator's application under the economic and social recovery plan, the user selecting a dedicated item in the payment menu and saving the receipt; a news report of the announcement rather than the tax directorate's own publication, with no start date, scope or volumes

subject: dpi.pay
name: Treasury electronic payment platform
milestone: Consolidated at one year of the technology strategy
position_start: Launched June 2025 to digitise state payments
position_end: Consolidated so that users pay taxes, fines and administrative fees by telephone in one secured system, with the first interoperability use cases on the national platform including public finances and an interconnection between the tax and customs directorates; the figures are the ministry's own with no independent measurement

subject: dpi.pay
name: Union complaints-handling circular
milestone: Binding on credit institutions, microfinance and electronic-money institutions
position_start: Requiring each institution to hold a complaints arrangement, answer within a month and handle complaints free of charge
position_end: Requiring each institution — electronic money issuers included — to hold a complaints arrangement proportionate to its size under a named officer and a written procedure, to inform customers of it in its premises, on its website and in contracts, to register every complaint and issue a receipt, to answer within a period not exceeding one month, and to handle complaints free of charge

subject: dpi.pay
name: Union external financial relations regulation
milestone: In force from signature 20 December 2024; application notes being issued
position_start: The 2010 regulation governing external financial relations
position_end: The 2024 regulation abrogates and replaces the 2010 one and is in force from signature; the central bank issued an application note in April 2026 specifying how external payments by foreign nationals holding union resident status are treated, so the implementing apparatus is being built out

subject: dpi.registry
name: Audit of civil registration in 74 communes
milestone: An audit mission launched at Rufisque 2026-07-28, covering 2018 to 2025
position_end: The mission live across 74 communes, 59 already audited and their findings re-examined, fifteen selected on risk analysis for document and field checks
note: it tests the reliability of the paper base the digital register is built on; no findings or reporting date are stated

subject: dpi.registry
name: Bill on computerising civil-status management
milestone: Listed among outstanding steps in the agency's August 2025 presentation
position_start: Drafted and validated, not adopted; the implementing decree unsigned
position_end: Still not adopted; no held source records adoption to 2026-08-06
note: validated is not enacted, and the register-reconstitution decree is likewise unsigned

subject: dpi.registry
name: Biometric audit of the public-service headcount
milestone: Physical and biometric enrolment running from 2026-06-23
position_end: More than 35 auditor teams deployed nationally with ten more to be added; the object is a reliable payroll database for wage-bill control
note: identity infrastructure whose beneficiary is the treasury; no correction or grievance route is stated for an agent the audit fails to find

subject: dpi.registry
name: Biometric register of artisanal gold miners
milestone: A convention signed 2026-07-30 by the mines ministry and the deposits fund
position_end: A convention signed, commissioning secured professional cards and a nationwide miner database
note: no enrolment target, timetable, cost, host, retention period or regulator role is stated, and the reported design carries no data-protection provision

subject: dpi.registry
name: Birth registration coverage
position_start: Just over 50% of under-fives registered (2013, EDS)
position_end: 81.4% of under-fives registered (EDS Continue 2023); the fifth census puts 5.3% of the whole population and 8.9% of under-fives without a birth certificate
note: Two instruments on different bases: a census stock figure and a survey coverage rate.

subject: dpi.registry
name: Business and association register
milestone: 26,685 new registrations in the fourth quarter of 2025
position_end: The statistics agency publishes a quarterly series of new registrations to the national register of enterprises and associations, which issues the taxpayer identification number: 26,685 in the fourth quarter of 2025, up 32.0% on the quarter and down 1.1% on the year, 76.0% of them sole traders; it is a flow series with no stock total published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Business registration platform
milestone: A digital platform launched for the enterprise and association identification number
position_end: Operating; no later state held at 2026-08-06
note: eighteen months with no update in the base; the object may have moved without the wiki holding it

subject: dpi.registry
name: Civil-registry digitisation system (LGEC)
milestone: Remediation running at Kaolack 10 to 20 August 2026
position_end: 471 of 629 civil-registry centres digitised, 43% activation of the citizen portal and 15,352,830 records centralised on pilot data at 13 July 2026, with a remediation push at Kaolack before extending to Kaffrine and Tambacounda
note: the figures are the civil-status agency's own pilot data; no national completion date is stated

subject: dpi.registry
name: Electoral register
milestone: 2025 ordinary revision completed, cards available from 2 June 2026
position_start: 7,371,890 registered voters at the 2024 presidential election, of whom 338,040 abroad
position_end: The 2025 ordinary revision completed, with cards from registrations, modifications and status changes available at prefectures on production of the deposit receipt and the biometric identity card; no revised national total is stated, and a May 2026 law narrowed the grounds for striking a citizen off and capped the resulting bar at five years

subject: dpi.registry
name: Land parcels surveyed and registered
milestone: 832,526 parcels surveyed at 30 June 2026, 157% of target
position_start: 673,000 parcels mapped and 469,000 carrying a cadastral identifier (2025-11)
position_end: 832,526 parcels surveyed at 30 June 2026 against a target of 157% met, 634,861 carrying a cadastral identifier, 550,072 deliberations validated and 441,315 parcels approved, with more than 70,000 women holding an occupancy title; 60 further communes signed second-phase conventions in May 2026 under a $40 million additional financing, and one commune received 10,318 occupancy titles in July 2026

subject: dpi.registry
name: National digital addressing project
milestone: Relaunch workshop opened 2026-08-05
position_end: Relaunched on an institutional footing: the workshop's deliverables are a governance structure, institutional responsibilities, an implementation roadmap and a monitoring framework, and the stated target is to complete the pilot phase within one year before national rollout
note: the government states the project made conceptual and technical progress in earlier years, but the base holds no position for it before the relaunch; no budget, lead implementing agency or pilot geography is stated

subject: dpi.registry
name: National education identifier
milestone: Nationwide deployment completed
position_end: An alphanumeric unique national registration number deployed nationwide for every actor in the education system, teacher and pupil alike, generated at enrolment by a sub-module of the ministry's platform; the fallback exchange route is spreadsheet export and import rather than a system-to-system interface

subject: dpi.registry
name: Single national social register coverage
milestone: The register reported rising from 542,000 to one million households over 2024
position_end: One million households (2024)
sources: 2025-12-09 Senegal's RNU social registry rises from 542,000 to one million households|2019-05-01 Senegal National Single Registry RNU (IPC-IG research brief 63)
note: reported in December 2025 and ingested in July 2026, so the growth is a 2024 event and not window movement; no later figure is held

subject: dpi.mis
name: Communal land information system
milestone: 55 communes integrated in preproduction at 30 June 2026
position_end: Development complete and the system in deployment: 55 communes integrated in preproduction and 112 of 128 communal land offices provisionally handed over at 30 June 2026, against a 2021 baseline in which the tax directorate's own land management system was only partly implemented and unconnected to municipal systems; preproduction is the operator's own word for the 55

subject: dpi.mis
name: Digital-health bill
milestone: A civil-society call for adoption at a restitution day 2026-07-23
position_end: Unadopted; status, sponsor and text not stated
note: the ministry has begun building a single patient record accessible to certified structures ahead of the law meant to govern confidentiality and transfer

subject: dpi.mis
name: Education statistics directorate mandate
milestone: Founded on a 1990 decree
position_start: Charged with a credible statistical information system and a forward-looking school map
position_end: Charged with a credible statistical information system and a forward-looking school map, coordinating the annual statistical campaign for the formal and non-formal sector and producing a national yearbook and indicators report annually; the mandate names no platform and publishes no coverage figure

subject: dpi.mis
name: Electronic port single window
milestone: Pilot for electronic release orders announced to open 2 January 2026
position_end: A pilot announced to open in January 2026 for electronic exchange of release orders through the port single window, automating transfer between the window and every terminal operator, following an electronic data interchange protocol signed in June 2025; the source records the announcement, not that the pilot went into production

subject: dpi.mis
name: GAINDÉ customs clearance system
milestone: Kidira office switched over 10 November 2025
position_start: Full dematerialisation of customs formalities in every connected unit from 1 January 2024
position_end: Full dematerialisation from 1 January 2024 in every connected unit, with electronic traceability and risk-scored targeting from the manifest onwards, extended in November 2025 to the Kidira office on the Dakar-Bamako corridor; the coverage limit is the connected units, not the whole territory

subject: dpi.mis
name: Higher-education ministry service digitisation
milestone: Further interoperability step announced by the ministry, August 2026
position_start: Did not exist as a recorded programme
position_end: The higher-education, research and innovation ministry reports a further step in the digital transformation of its services, framed around interoperability; no service list, user count or completion date is on file

subject: dpi.mis
name: KIX-SEEDS education data systems project
milestone: Issue brief published December 2025
position_end: A GPE/KIX-funded project coordinated by APHRC with HISP Uganda, ESEA Senegal and ISSP Burkina Faso as country implementing partners, working on sub-national education-data collection, quality and use; a year of work was reviewed at the Ouagadougou annual general meeting of June 2025 and an issue brief published in December 2025. No budget, end date or coverage figure is on the record
note: Runs across Uganda, Senegal and Burkina Faso together.

subject: dpi.mis
name: Mortality and cause-of-death analysis tool
milestone: A health-ministry training workshop held on 20 and 21 July 2026
position_end: Training delivered; the tool assesses mortality data coded to international classifications and disaggregates by age, sex, territory and cause
note: cause-of-death quality worked on inside the health information system rather than through the civil register

subject: dpi.mis
name: SEN-CORS national geodetic network
milestone: 22 permanent stations operational
position_end: 22 permanent satellite-positioning stations across the territory serving as the national geodetic reference frame for land registration, the cadastre and spatial planning, with data, download and supervision tools published to surveyers, state technical services and local authorities

subject: dpi.mis
name: SIMEN education management platform
status: Implemented, reaching about a fifth of schools
milestone: Coverage stated in the KIX-SEEDS issue brief, December 2025
position_end: Comprehensive in design but reaching only about 20% of schools, held back by weak system integration and connectivity; collection is largely manual and paper-based alongside isolated digital files, with no real-time dashboards or standardised protocols, and over a third of public schools lack electricity while only a quarter have internet access
note: Coverage and school-infrastructure figures are the brief’s own citations of Education Profiles (2024) and ICTworks (2023).

subject: dpi.mis
name: Social protection information systems
milestone: Draft decrees amending the register and the family security grant scheme adopted 16 July 2026
position_start: A single register operational since 2015 at about 550,000 households, with beneficiary management drawing targeting from it and grant payments still made through the post office
position_end: The register extended to 996,194 households, and the Council of Ministers adopted in July 2026 a social protection framework bill and draft decrees amending both the family security grant scheme and the 2021 decree creating the register; the register's monitoring committee, its procedures manual and the pilot digitisation of grant payment were all still outstanding in June 2026

subject: dpi.mis
name: Tax administration digital platforms
milestone: Five tele-procedure platforms in service; an integrated application in development
position_end: Five distinct hosted applications in service — online declaration and payment, a personal space for individuals and small firms, financial-statement filing, the compliance levy and an e-services form — with an integrated application named as under development to serve every category of taxpayer

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Citizen single window
milestone: The portal launched by the prime minister 2026-03-24 and declared operational
position_end: Operational for passport applications, business creation, police-clearance and nationality certificates, with online tracking
note: unveiled alongside a sovereignty cloud, a unified government payment system and a consular platform

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Digital fiscal stamp
milestone: The tax authority withdrew the paper stamp on 2026-07-20, making the digital service the sole recognised channel
position_end: The sole recognised channel nationwide, with QR-coded stamps bought and received remotely and a second access route through a super-app
note: this is removal of the analogue channel rather than addition of a digital one; unused paper stamps were exchangeable until 2026-08-15, and no offline or assisted route is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: e-Justice court digitisation programme
status: Piloting, official launch set for 10 September 2026
milestone: Official launch announced for 10 September 2026
position_end: The justice ministry announced that e-Justice and a second platform, Jokkoo ak Yoon, would be officially launched on 10 September 2026 to dematerialise judicial procedures, strengthen their traceability and ease exchanges between courts and citizens. Carried by the Directorate of Dematerialisation and Digital Automation with United Nations development support, e-Justice is to bring case enrolment, management of the general roll, prosecution and registry activity, investigation and the handling of appeals into one digital environment, with the Pikine-Guediawaye high court among the pilot jurisdictions and reduced processing times the stated aim
note: the second platform's own scope is not set out beyond easing exchanges between courts and citizens, and no court count, case volume, cost or rollout schedule accompanies the launch date

subject: dpi.govtech
name: e-Sénégal single-window portal
milestone: Launched 24 March 2026, authenticating on the national identification number
position_end: Launched by the state digital operator and accessed by authentication on the national identification number carried on the biometric card, with criminal record, nationality certificate, prison visit authorisation and public-service non-membership certificates live, civil-status acts and urbanism procedures to follow, and mobile money and card payment of fees

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic fiscal stamp platform
milestone: Sole official platform from 20 July 2026
position_end: The sole official platform for acquiring and consuming fiscal stamps from 20 July 2026, administered wholly by the tax directorate's own services, with purchase and payment from a phone, the stamp issued electronically with a unique code and needing no printing, and a transition window to 15 August for holders of unused physical stamps

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Free electronic fiscal-stamp service
milestone: The provider suspended its free tier on 2026-07-28, citing an administrative decision outside its control
position_start: A free stamp and passport-receipt distribution service, running six years
position_end: The free tier suspended, with refunds promised within 72 hours; users state they now pay additional fees for an identical service
note: the first consumer-cost consequence of state-platform exclusivity the wiki holds; it is not stated whether the decision was addressed to the provider or to the distribution channel generally

subject: dpi.govtech
name: National Assembly SIPOP system
milestone: Equipment tender opened 2026-08-05
position_end: IT equipment out to tender by the United Nations development programme for the Assembly's SIPOP system; what the system does, its value and its timetable are not stated in the notice
note: the base holds only the procurement notice, so the parliamentary system itself is unestablished: no function, scope or go-live is on record

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Public procurement platform APPEL
milestone: Launched 2025-10-15 to carry state acquisition procedures
position_end: Operating as the state's electronic procurement channel; the procurement regulator's director-general states it is intended to capture the procedures of a thousand administrations and names its protection as a priority alongside critical state digital infrastructure
note: no count of administrations onboarded, procurement volume, availability record or security accreditation is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Regulator digital platforms
milestone: Eight platforms deployed by the telecommunications regulator
position_end: Eight platforms live, including a national digital-infrastructure map and a tariff platform
note: sovereignty-framed modernisation; no usage or publication figures are held

subject: digital.localgov
name: Building-permit and administrative-acts platform
milestone: Over 200,000 permit files digitised
position_end: More than 200,000 building-permit files digitised and the physical archives of the region's urbanism directorates secured; the platform dematerialises the permit procedure across Dakar, Pikine, Guédiawaye and Rufisque, extended to the region's 52 communes and 10 sub-prefectures, and now carries dozens of procedures across other sectors

subject: digital.localgov
name: Commune-level systems other than civil status
milestone: Local-finances observatory opened 23 July 2026 over 601 local authorities
position_end: A Treasury platform centralising the budgetary, accounting and financial records of all 601 local authorities opened in July 2026; a building-permit platform covering the Dakar region has digitised over 200,000 permit files; a 2024 convention commits the state operator to supply mail management, domain names, hosting and revenue-collection software to the 557 communes; and a six-commune administration digitalisation pilot opened in April 2026
note: the subject's four sources are all civil-registration items already carried as registry objects; nothing on municipal financial management, local revenue platforms or commune open data

subject: digital.localgov
name: Digital inclusion volunteer placements
milestone: Eight-month pilot launched 2 September 2025 across 24 communes
position_end: About twenty volunteers trained in digital archiving, maintenance and solution development placed across 24 communes in seven departments for eight months, financed at EUR 24,423; a small externally funded pilot rather than a state records programme

subject: digital.localgov
name: Local finances observatory
milestone: Opened 23 July 2026
position_end: A Treasury platform centralising, securing, analysing and publishing the budgetary, accounting and financial records of the 601 local authorities, which the Treasury states were until then dispersed and hard to exploit; it carries a search engine and is to be interconnected progressively with other state systems, with taxpayer self-registration and mobile payment to follow

subject: digital.localgov
name: Public administration digitalisation project
milestone: Pilot phase launched at Mbour 24 April 2026 across six communes
position_end: A pilot across six communes — Mbour, Dakar-Plateau, Ngor, Rufisque, Kaffrine and Kaolack — consolidating network and digital infrastructure, digitalising public services and securing the service offer; six communes is the whole of the current perimeter

subject: digital.localgov
name: Satellite connectivity for local institutions
milestone: Kits installed at three Bignona institutions 9 April 2026
position_end: Very-high-speed satellite kits installed at two vocational training centres and the Bignona town hall under the universal connectivity policy, with the departmental council asked to draw up a territorial digital plan identifying uncovered zones

subject: digital.rural
name: Connectivity and equipment at the deconcentrated service centres
milestone: Regional tour closed at Matam, 3 September 2026
position_end: The director of the state's deconcentrated service network said on 3 September 2026, closing a tour of four regions, that without connectivity there can be no deconcentration of public services. He listed connectivity, workstations, IT equipment, archive and mail management and communications security among the problems found in prefectures and gendarmerie posts, and announced the forthcoming integration of civil registration and further functions into the national dematerialisation platform alongside a national digital-government launch
note: the head of the network stating that its precondition is missing is the finding; no centre count, connectivity rate, equipment gap or remediation budget is published against it

subject: digital.rural
name: Digital data capture in rural health facilities
milestone: 73% of 300,000 planned computerised patient records completed at December 2025
position_end: The routine national health platform collects from health-post level upward, with a community pilot covering about 803 health huts using mobile modules; 73% of the 300,000 planned computerised patient records were reported done in December 2025, a national figure with no rural breakdown, and a health programme appraised in February 2026 finances electronic medical records and interoperability tools aimed at isolated and rural populations

subject: digital.rural
name: Online civil-status certificate platform
milestone: Brought into service at Mbacké 16 February 2026, five pilot communes
position_end: Online applications for birth, death and marriage certificates delivered to a phone or computer, in a four-week test across five pilot communes before extension; any centre wanting it must first install the central civil-status management software

subject: digital.rural
name: Online cybercrime reporting platform
milestone: Launched 12 February 2026, in test phase
position_end: Built in-house by police engineers and housed at the special cybercrime division, letting users report without attending a station; presented as a step toward dematerialising procedures and interconnecting police databases, and functional in a test phase at launch

subject: digital.rural
name: Rural digital data capture
milestone: 400 civil-registration centres interconnected at programme close, June 2026
position_end: Civil registration is the furthest advanced: 400 centres interconnected, 10 million records digitised and 20 million indexed at the close of the modernisation programme, and an online certificate platform in service at Mbacké from February 2026 in five pilot communes. Health data capture rests on the routine national platform from health-post level, with a community pilot covering about 803 health huts. A national online cybercrime reporting channel opened in February 2026
note: the subject's only substantive holding is the satellite-kit connectivity programme, which belongs to the connectivity section; nothing on rural enumeration, agricultural census digitisation or field-level capture

subject: tech.ai
name: Algorithmic tax audit selection
milestone: Field experiment across tax offices, half the audit programme algorithm-selected
position_end: A risk-scoring algorithm built on newly digitised micro data selected half the annual corporate audit programme against inspector selection for the other half, and the trial reported against it: inspector-selected audits were 18 percentage points more likely to be conducted and detected 89% more evasion, and algorithm-selected audits were less cost-effective and did not reduce corruption

subject: tech.ai
name: Artificial intelligence in sectoral information systems
milestone: Cadastral mass-valuation under experiment; a health systematic review launched September 2025
position_end: Under experiment rather than deployed: the cadastre is testing artificial intelligence for a mass-valuation system to widen the property-tax base alongside an automated parcel-identifier platform in test across its offices, a partner institute's crop-mapping chain produces 10-metre crop maps and in-season forecasts for groundnut and millet, and the health ministry launched a systematic review in September 2025 that produced a strategy document rather than a deployed module

subject: tech.ai
name: Data protection commission position on manipulated media
milestone: Communiqué of 7 October 2025
position_end: The regulator recorded the circulation of generated videos and images featuring public figures, religious leaders and ordinary citizens without consent, condemned the practice and stated that those responsible are exposed to the sanctions the law provides, naming mass collection without knowledge, identity usurpation, information manipulation and reputationally damaging deepfakes as the risks
note: the commission's own page serves no article body; a press report of the communiqué stands in its place

subject: tech.ai
name: Dedicated AI legislation
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-10 - a four-country comparative study found no AI-specific legislation in force or in draft
milestone: No AI-specific instrument on record
position_end: None published
note: the strategy stack and the ethics committee carry the field; the study rates Cote d'Ivoire's strategy the most advanced of the four on inclusion and data governance

subject: tech.ai
name: National AI ethics committee
milestone: A readiness assessment records an ethics committee as planned
position_end: Planned; no statute, membership, chair or date
note: the assessment is dated 2025 with no month, so the date here is the reporting date; the full report is not held

subject: tech.ai
name: Place in an AI readiness index
note: Senegal is absent from the eight African states ranked in the 2026 edition, so this is an absence from the index rather than a low score

subject: tech.ai
name: Press code provisions on manipulated content
milestone: In force since 2017-07-13
position_start: Forbidding distortion of a text, document, image or sound and requiring montages to be flagged
position_end: Article 13 forbids distorting a text, document, image or sound and requires image, sound and archive montages to be flagged; article 14 forbids journalists and media technicians from manipulating images to falsify them; article 17 makes publishing a montage made with a person's words or image without consent an invasion of privacy. The code is technology-neutral and names neither artificial intelligence nor deepfakes, and its scope is the press and audiovisual and online communication

subject: tech.ai
name: Senegal AI Factory
milestone: Korean project-management tender issued 2026-08-31, bids close 2026-10-20
position_end: KOICA issued an international project-management tender on 31 August 2026 for a Senegal AI transformation centre and digital capacity-building project, with bidding opening on 18 October and closing on 20 October 2026
note: the meeting carries no date of its own, so the publication date is used; the topics the delegation discussed — trustworthy-AI governance, compute infrastructure, innovation financing and partnerships — are the things the programme is not yet reported to have

subject: tech.ai
name: Wolof and French AI tutor by phone call
milestone: Presented at a national prize ceremony 2026-07-30
position_end: A tutor reachable by ordinary phone call with no internet, curriculum written by teachers and validated by school inspectors, hosted on servers in Senegal
note: no user, pricing, call-cost, contract or evaluation figures are given, and the education ministry's role is asserted by the vendor rather than confirmed by it

subject: tech.industry
name: Acquisition of a Senegalese health-technology company
milestone: Acquired by a French insurance technology company, September 2026
position_end: Acquired in what the account calls a rare francophone health-technology exit; no price, range or split is disclosed and the company's revenue was withheld (2026-09)
note: No deal value is taken from this source and none is stated anywhere.

subject: tech.industry
name: Senegal Digital Factory FabLab network
milestone: First laboratory announced for inauguration 27 April 2026
position_end: The first laboratory of the network announced for inauguration at a Diamniadio university, housing facilities for manufacturing phone shells by three-dimensional printing and software modelling and for developing agriculture and health solutions, with the stated objective of reducing imports of digital products; the network is to extend to the country's eight economic poles

subject: tech.innovate
name: Corporate mobility platform
milestone: Launched in Senegal 2026-07-16
position_end: A centralised platform for companies to manage employee travel, set spending limits, automate billing and track rides in real time
note: the claimed cost reduction is the company's own

subject: tech.innovate
name: Digital technology park at Diamniadio
milestone: Works restarted 3 November 2025 with phase one due March 2026
position_end: Works officially restarted with the government committing to deliver a first phase of 12.5 hectares by March 2026 — three towers for technology firms, startups and investors, a research centre run with universities, an incubation centre, an audiovisual production centre and a training centre; it establishes a restart and a target date, not a commissioning

subject: tech.innovate
name: Max it super-app on the Dakar rapid-transit network
milestone: The transit operator and the telecommunications operator signed a partnership 2026-07-14
position_start: Ticketing available through the operator's money service since commercial launch in May 2024, with the super-app not integrated
position_end: An agreement signed for progressive integration of ticketing, subscription top-ups and further services, with transport-card top-ups, bank financing, station Wi-Fi and passenger-flow analytics planned
note: progressive and eventual throughout, with no go-live date or phasing published

subject: tech.innovate
name: Startup Act implementing decree and accreditation route
milestone: Accreditation platform opened 20 November 2025
position_start: The implementing decree creating an evaluation, support and coordination commission accrediting support structures
position_end: The accreditation platform opened in November 2025, which the minister described as moving the startup law into implementation; the decree requires support structures to be accredited through a dematerialised procedure valid three years, sets their duties and eligibility, and creates a startup label and a promotion fund with loan and equity mechanisms under an 80% state guarantee quota

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Civil-service e-training project
milestone: Four training guides validated and an e-module tested January 2026
position_end: Four structuring guides validated at the national school of administration in January 2026 — trainer training, running of placements, drafting of practical cases and organisation of entrance examinations — and a project-management module tested with about twenty serving civil servants and students; no figure for civil servants trained is published

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Digital financial-education project
milestone: The project closed 2026-07-15, with a closing workshop on 2026-07-23
position_start: Running since June 2024 in Senegal and Cameroon
position_end: Closed, with 265 civil-society trainers trained across twelve organisations in two cities, and a comparison platform left unmaintained because no implementer can compel tariff data from financial institutions
note: the wiki held nothing on it before 2026-07-24, so the whole life-cycle arrives as one closing item

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Digital Schools programme
milestone: A memorandum signed to equip 120 primary schools and train 500 women at seven digital houses
position_start: The memorandum signed: 120 schools and 500 women targeted
position_end: Unchanged; no schools-equipped or women-trained count is held at any date
note: the position is identical at both ends of the window, and this is the wiki's only school-level digital-literacy instrument for Senegal

subject: capacity.literacy
name: FORCE N digital and artificial-intelligence teacher training
milestone: Over 3,000 teachers certified 2026-02-18 against 105,000 announced
position_end: Over 3,000 teachers certified in digital competences and artificial intelligence in a pilot phase, against the 105,000 announced in September 2025 and a corps of 111,000, with the education ministry seeking to make the training compulsory

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Satellite connectivity for primary schools
milestone: Plan announced 2026-08-26
position_end: an education ministry plan to connect more than 8,000 primary schools to the internet by satellite

subject: capacity.training
name: Sovereign-cloud engineer training
milestone: The digital minister states the infrastructure is deployed and tested and that training has not started
position_end: About 100 engineers to be trained in advanced cloud technologies, with infrastructure in testing and training not begun
note: no contract, value or schedule is held

subject: capacity.training
name: Statistician graduates from the national statistics school
position_end: 60 graduates in 2026 - 33 statistician-economists and 27 statistician-analysts - from a cumulative output above 900 since 2011
note: the 2026 cohort drew students from ten African countries; the national statistics agency used the graduation to press ministries to recruit them into sectoral statistical services, which states an absorption problem without measuring it - no figure is published for how many of the 900 are employed in Senegalese public statistics

subject: capacity.training
name: Young Africa Works Senegal
milestone: A US$200m five-year commitment announced September 2019
position_start: US$200m committed, the programme running to 2030
position_end: US$200m committed; no disbursement, beneficiary or mid-term figure is held
note: the largest single skills commitment in the base, and seven years in the wiki holds no evidence of delivery

subject: capacity.research
name: National research and innovation fund
milestone: A council of ministers communiqué proposes the fund alongside applied research laboratories
position_end: Proposed; no budget, statute or date, with a companion council still at reflection stage
note: none of the proposals is an adopted instrument

subject: capacity.research
name: Regional mathematics and artificial intelligence institute memorandum
milestone: Signed at Mbour, 10 December 2025
position_start: No cross-border artificial intelligence teaching arrangement (2025-08)
position_end: A memorandum signed at Mbour on 10 December 2025 sets a roadmap toward a satellite centre for advanced mathematics and artificial intelligence, with no site or funding attached (2025-12)

subject: capacity.research
name: Two AI research laboratories
milestone: Both laboratories launched 2025-01-31 with three ministers present
position_start: Two laboratories launched, targeting agriculture, education and industry
position_end: Unchanged; no publication, budget, headcount or research output is held
note: the only standing AI research infrastructure the wiki holds for Senegal, and eighteen months with no follow-up item

subject: include.access
name: Asylum application and documentation route
milestone: Applications lodged with the national eligibility commission at Dakar
position_end: Applications lodged with the national eligibility commission at Dakar on a form with an individual signed request and four photographs; on deposit the applicant receives a six-month renewable receipt permitting free movement pending decision, followed by two interviews, with refusal appealable to the commission and then to the President

subject: include.access
name: Digital training for blind and partially sighted people
milestone: An advanced-level course launched 2026-07-06
position_end: 700 blind and partially sighted people and twenty trainers trained since the programme's launch, with an advanced tier now running
note: the programme's start date is not stated, so the cumulative figure has no start point, and no funding figure or state role is reported

subject: include.access
name: Médiateur de la République
milestone: 72 complaints received in the fourth quarter of 2025
position_end: The standing national channel through which any person may complain about a state administration, a local authority or a body charged with a public-service mission, free of charge, its powers limited to recommendation and investigation with no coercive power; it received 72 complaints in the fourth quarter of 2025, 63 still with the administrations concerned, land matters the largest subject at 23

subject: include.access
name: National dialogue day consultations
milestone: First cycle of consultations opened 21 May 2026
position_end: Opened as a fixture of the republican agenda, its first cycle consulting six former prime ministers with consultations to continue with other representative figures; it is evidence of a consultation mechanism rather than of citizen participation, and names no platform, timetable or published output

subject: include.access
name: National gender equity and equality strategy
milestone: Second-generation strategy covering 2016 to 2026
position_start: The standing national gender-equity instrument, covering disparity by sector with a logical framework to 2026
position_end: The standing national gender-equity instrument, covering disparity by sector with a logical framework running to 2026; it provides the national frame for sex-disaggregated data and gender-responsive budgeting but sets no quantitative indicator on digital or information-technology access

subject: include.access
name: Oil and gas sector grievance mechanism
milestone: Launch workshop held 17 March 2026
position_end: A multi-channel state grievance mechanism — messaging application, e-mail, web form and physical boxes — open to populations, workers and community organisations, with named principles of accessibility, confidentiality and personal-data protection; its scope is the oil and gas sector tied to two producing projects, not a whole-of-government portal

subject: include.access
name: Regional humanitarian initiative for displaced people
milestone: Launched at Dakar 29 January 2026, FCFA 313,083,755 over nine months
position_end: A regional initiative of FCFA 313,083,755 over nine months for refugees, internally displaced, stateless people and asylum seekers, implemented with the refugee agency's Dakar office and a local foundation, targeting displaced communities of Casamance and Mauritanian refugees in the river valley across education, livelihoods, health, vocational training and social assistance; no beneficiary count is given

subject: include.access
name: Un étudiant, un ordinateur student-computer programme
milestone: Commission of inquiry opened 129-0 on 2026-08-20
position_end: Under a parliamentary commission of inquiry covering about 48 billion FCFA of commitments since 2017
note: the National Assembly voted 129-0 to open a commission of inquiry into roughly 48 billion FCFA committed since 2017, on alleged breaches of the public procurement code, a guarantee fund of about 2 billion FCFA with a commercial bank, and 800 defective computers stored unused at Cheikh Anta Diop University; no device-delivery total, cost per unit or student-reach figure is published for the programme, so the inquiry's envelope is the only quantity the base holds about it

subject: include.access
name: Women's digital skills programmes
milestone: 560 trained across seven centres at a 50% female split; a 200-entrepreneur agreement signed November 2025
position_end: 560 participants trained across seven centres in five-day cohorts, of whom 50% were female, in computer basics, digital awareness and introductory artificial intelligence; and an agreement signed with the telecommunications regulator in November 2025 to train 200 young women entrepreneurs in digital solutions, with no value, duration or start date stated

subject: include.divides
name: Domestic measurement of the digital divide or digital literacy
note: every divide figure on file comes from a reference study and none is promoted here

subject: include.divides
name: Population without connectivity
position_end: 40% of the population still without access to connectivity, on the minister's statement to parliament (2026-08)
note: stated by the telecommunications minister during the critical-infrastructure bill's debate and attributed to a 2024 sector diagnosis of coverage gaps and unmet operator obligations; the diagnosis itself is not held, no definition of access is given, and the figure is two years old at the point of its citation

subject: data.statistics
name: Civil-status agency statistical mandate
milestone: Interoperability protocol with the statistics agency signed 23 January 2026
position_end: The agency is charged with producing a statistical yearbook of civil-status data and transmitting civil-status data to the statistical services, with a centralised national and consular database to be interfaced with other producers' databases; an interoperability protocol with the statistics agency was signed in January 2026, its scope, data categories and timetable unpublished

subject: data.statistics
name: Inclusive-data initiative second phase
milestone: The national statistics agency hosted the first second-phase peer exchange in Dakar
position_end: The second phase opened, widening from three countries to five
note: a month-precision date; the exchange's exact dates are not published

subject: data.statistics
name: National strategy for the development of statistics
status: Implemented, the operative edition's text is not held
milestone: Third strategy expired 2023; a fourth is referenced and under revision
position_start: The third strategy, dated December 2019, is the latest full text obtainable
position_end: The third strategy, dated December 2019, is the latest full text obtainable; its own period expired in 2023, a fourth covering 2024 to 2028 is referenced as published in October 2025 and its revision was launched on 27 March 2026, and no decree adopting any edition was found

subject: data.statistics
name: Report on the observance of standards and codes for macroeconomic statistics
milestone: Report published; recommendations accepted
position_end: An International Monetary Fund report found the country's macroeconomic statistics generally reliable but the statistical system operating at two speeds: it credited the statistics agency, the regional central bank and the finance ministry while finding sector-specific statistical agencies constrained by staffing and finance. It recommended a clearer coordination mandate for the statistics agency through a permanent inter-agency committee reconciling national accounts, public finance, debt, monetary and external-sector figures before publication, broader public-debt reporting covering accounts payable and pension obligations, and steps toward the enhanced data dissemination standard. The country has subscribed to the general standard since November 2017 and the authorities accepted the recommendations under the 2024-2028 national statistical development strategy
note: acceptance is recorded and delivery is not: no dated commitment, committee, instrument or reporting change is published against any of the recommendations

subject: data.open
name: National data archive catalogue
status: Implemented, a licensed catalogue rather than an open-licence portal
milestone: Per-dataset consultation counts published
position_end: The only Senegalese public-data system publishing per-dataset consultation counts — 4,808,203 views on the 2013 census, 24,422 on the 2024-2025 agricultural survey, 19,910 on the 2023 census — with access stated per dataset as licensed or withheld, so views are not downloads and the archive is not an open-licence portal

subject: data.open
name: Open government data framework and portals
status: In development, committed in the data strategy with no adopting instrument
milestone: Statistical open-data platform extended to the regions from June 2026
position_end: No standalone open-data charter, law or decree; the 2023-2028 data strategy commits to a legal framework for data opening and a national publication platform, a national geoportal launched in November 2025, and the statistics agency is extending its own open-data platform to the regions
note: the only two sources carrying the subject are a blog on post-donor data systems and the regulator's internal tool suite, neither of which is an open-data instrument

subject: data.satellite
name: Agro-pastoral campaign monitoring bulletin
milestone: Bulletin 17 of a standing series, end of the 2023 season
position_start: A standing series analysing the vegetation index against a 1999-2022 historical baseline
position_end: A standing series analysing the vegetation index from June to October against the 1999-2022 historical minimum, maximum and mean, combined with field data and a tested plant-production model, yielding a plant-production map and a fodder balance for the pastoral zones

subject: data.satellite
name: Earth observation in agricultural statistics
milestone: Five-year framework agreement signed February 2026
position_end: A five-year framework agreement to develop methods calculating area under cultivation, crop types and seasonal yields from Earth observation alongside field surveys, with technical support focused on rice, groundnut, millet and maize; no value, workplan or start date beyond the signature is stated

subject: data.satellite
name: Meteorological satellite reception and nowcasting
milestone: Named regional specialised centre for West African nowcasting, May 2026
position_start: Forecasters accessing European satellite products through a ground receiver, satellite data compensating for a low-density observation network
position_end: Named the regional specialised meteorological centre producing nowcasting products for West Africa under a new satellite application facility, with near-real-time third-generation imagery in use and lightning-imager data described as critical in the rainy season; a United States early-warning project also opened at Dakar in January 2026 with Senegal among five pilot countries

subject: data.satellite
name: Rice remote-sensing monitoring pilot
milestone: Platform piloted with the national agricultural research institute
position_end: A platform combining radar and optical satellite imagery with ground information and a crop-growth model to map rice area, track seasons and simulate yields in the Senegal River valley and Casamance, run with the national agricultural research institute rather than the statistical service

subject: data.satellite
name: Satellite data in public administration
milestone: Framework agreement bringing satellite data into agricultural statistics, February 2026
